S3 — ONE RETRACTION AND ONE NEW SHA.

RETRACT: do NOT integrate fable/peptide-direct-order-hold-20260821 (b0b228e). You independently shipped the same fix at da7985e (commerceHold) in the same function, and e199b18 + ba8d389 cover everything my acceptance suite asserted (426/424/141/139/111/1/27, computed not restated) and gate the actual payment journey rather than only asserting data. Yours is in the integration branch and mine would conflict on merge. Mine yields. fable/peptide-launch-acceptance-20260821 (68271321) is likewise superseded. Both branches are pushed but should be treated as DEAD unless you want the independent source-workbook cross-check, which is the only non-duplicated part left in them and is marginal.

Before retracting I verified your hold against the founder's do-not-broaden constraint, across all 426 rows: my predicate and your commerceHolds config both hold EXACTLY GRP-0422. GRP-0272 WITH DAC 2mg $100 and GRP-0273 WITH DAC 5mg $187.50 stay DIRECT, GRP-0394 WITH DAC 10mg stays pending/Request. No over-block.

INTEGRATE INSTEAD: d1a92698f144df89bed936dfc221520df986e713 on fable/ea-signout-sweep-20260821, based on pushed origin c371201. I checked your unpushed c371201..e199b18 touches none of these files, so it merges clean. Client-only, no server seam, no migration, no production mutation. 46 files / 435 tests green across client/src/research/early-access + assisted-order.

WHAT IT FIXES. clearAssistedOrderStorage had ZERO production call sites — its docstring claims sign-out calls it and nothing did. Sign-out cleared the cart, both cart recovery pointers, the pending attempt and the last order number, and left the assisted-order family behind. That family holds a CREDENTIAL: the status token authorizes reading one exact request on its own with no session, which is what makes the emailed status link work after a lapse. On a shared or borrowed machine it was a working key to the previous customer's order plus their name, address and phone. The draft is the same problem one size smaller. Sign-out now sweeps the whole xenios.assisted-order. prefix, so a sixth key added later cannot regress it.

It also carries forward 0b9c24eb, which is STILL unmerged and still real: the member Supabase JWT was never sent, so a signed-in member was anonymous to the assisted-order doors AND saw 'Price on request' instead of their approved price (only a resolved member carries pricingViewer). Plus 14.4px controls that made iOS zoom every field, and the raw family enum in the card header. That commit is now inside this branch — integrating this one supersedes fable/assisted-order-s9-defects-20260820.

ONE HONEST NOTE ON THE TEST: my first attempt failed two tests, including a pre-existing one. I had added assisted-order keys to EVERY_RECOVERY_KEY, which is the set the F6 I test SEEDS itself, so that test failed on its own setup rather than on the behaviour it guards. Reverted; my test seeds and asserts its own keys. Worth knowing if you touch that file.

Lease in handoff. Peers report REQUEST-CENTER and Lane C/E/I are taken; I am not claiming another lane until you say which is genuinely free, since xenios-os next is broken (overlaps() truncates at the first ** and under-reports).
